source.title: Non-Euclidean Gradient Descent Operates at the Edge of Stability
source.authors: Rustem Islamov; M. Crawshaw; Jeremy Cohen; Robert M. Gower

record.tranche_reason: Tests edge-of-stability behavior using generalized sharpness and directional smoothness for several non-Euclidean gradient methods, and compares quadratic Taylor dynamics before and during EoS.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for generalized sharpness and loss dynamics. The standard Euclidean sharpness results are included where explicitly described. Initialization, width, depth-without-shortcuts, training classification error, and the other listed claim versions are not tested.
record.test_reason: Figure 1 directly tests V5's full-batch GD edge-of-stability component using training loss and the largest Hessian eigenvalue on CIFAR-10-5k. These experiments use the original method and measure; the main non-Euclidean experiments extend the question using different curvature quantities.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors propose geometry-dependent generalized sharpness and observe sharpening followed by near-threshold or slightly above-threshold plateaus across several non-Euclidean methods. Standard Euclidean sharpness can miss these dynamics. Their quadratic analysis proves convergence below threshold and constructs divergence above it for a particular initialization and valid dual-gradient selection; generic divergence and the pre-EoS oscillatory regime remain unexplained.
record.recipe_differences: Studies full-batch non-Euclidean gradient methods and generalized sharpness, with Euclidean GD as a consistency case; it does not reproduce the specific large-learning-rate catapult recipe in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: Behavior and measured threshold depend on update geometry and sharpness definition; non-Euclidean methods can show pre-EoS oscillations, and estimated generalized sharpness can depend on Frank-Wolfe restarts for some norms.

fits_no_version.finding: Non-Euclidean methods exhibit progressive sharpening and threshold plateaus for curvature measured in their update geometry; normalized methods require division by the dual gradient norm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Full-batch non-Euclidean gradient methods can exhibit edge-of-stability behavior in geometry-dependent generalized sharpness, including when standard Euclidean sharpness remains below 2/η.

fits_no_version.finding: The frozen quadratic approximation tracks real-objective dynamics before EoS but diverges during EoS under Spectral GD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-Euclidean neural-network training can remain bounded where the corresponding local quadratic dynamics diverge.

fits_no_version.finding: Under ℓ∞-descent, predictions begin oscillating around step 300 while generalized sharpness remains below threshold; EoS follows around step 450.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some non-Euclidean gradient methods have a bounded oscillatory regime before generalized sharpness reaches the stability threshold.

record.problems: The text reports plotted trajectories without numeric uncertainty estimates. Generalized sharpness for some norms is a multi-restart Frank-Wolfe estimate and may underestimate the global maximum when too few restarts are used. The quadratic divergence experiment is empirical, while the theory establishes divergence only for a specific initialization in general non-Euclidean norms.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately described outcome rows were omitted. Several figure panels are recorded as figure-only because the text does not provide exact values.

untested.parts: Training classification error approaching zero, random or corrupted labels, and model-size, stopping, or regularization effects.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious minima, and extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and prevention by identity shortcuts or special training recipes.
Comparisons of initialization, signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth. Frank-Wolfe restarts concern a diagnostic estimator, not network initialization.

Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, the catapult loss rise and curvature drop, width dependence, divergence at larger initial rates, and actual training divergence despite starting below threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on speed or learning-rate tolerance and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source listed for V5. Its non-Euclidean findings extend the standard GD claim rather than limiting it directly. Quadratic-surrogate divergence and limitations of the new theory do not justify the record's limits_scope verdict. States marked cannot_determine for unlinked rows concern their ability to establish an existing claim version, not whether their reported non-Euclidean effects occurred.

versions.untested_parts: Near-zero training classification error, corrupted or random labels, and the effects of model size, training duration, early stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth effects on training error, residual shortcuts, special initialization, and normalization-free residual training.
Initialization choices, signal or gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Does not test learning rates above the initial linearized stability limit in the specific catapult setup, wide-network scaling, or the claim about some below-threshold runs diverging.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, or Fixup training without normalization.

rows.subject: CNN
rows.operation_detail: Switched from the real objective to its quadratic Taylor approximation at selected iterations during Spectral GD.

conditions.value: Four marked iterations; exact values not stated in text

rows.measure: Loss dynamics on the quadratic approximation compared with the real objective.
rows.value: Before EoS, the quadratic approximation closely tracks the real loss; during EoS, it quickly diverges.
rows.note: The paper interprets this as supporting a connection between generalized sharpness near 2/η and divergence on the local quadratic approximation.
rows.check: Divergence occurs after replacing the neural-network objective with a frozen quadratic approximation. This does not demonstrate divergence of the actual training run or test V5's initial learning-rate recovery claim.

rows.subject: fully connected network
rows.operation_detail: Measured generalized sharpness, directional smoothness, and network predictions during ℓ∞-descent.
rows.measure: Generalized sharpness and directional smoothness relative to 2/η; prediction oscillation.
rows.baseline: Initially generalized sharpness is less than 2/η, directional smoothness is ≈ 0, and predictions are not oscillating.
rows.value: Around step 300, generalized sharpness is still less than 2/η while directional smoothness rises and predictions start oscillating; around step 450 both measures reach 2/η.
rows.note: This reports a pre-EoS oscillatory regime, an additional qualification to the usual threshold description.
rows.check: Pre-threshold prediction oscillations under ℓ∞-descent concern a non-Euclidean intermediate regime. They establish neither below-threshold divergence nor failure of the standard GD sharpness plateau in V5. Remove the malformed numbers_found value.
